abstractions: USDS/sUSDS/phUSD/pair/factory/router are trivial axiomatized stubs (approve->true, deposit no-op, getPair returns a symbolic address, token0/token1 symbolic). No OZ/UniV2 behaviour is proven.
Mock pair.sync() reverts with a unique SyncSentinel() so 'sync reached' is observable; hence _swapAmount/sqrt and quotePool are never executed (out of scope by brief).
Donation path disabled (psm == 0): _psmDonate divisions never reached.
_defaultHook is private immutable with no getter: observed behaviourally through whether dispatch reverts UniPoolerV2__HookNotSet.

proofs.claim: hook == constructor default, symbolic minter m!=0 wired + unpaused, symbolic amount/extraData => dispatch reverts with exactly the 4-byte UniPoolerV2__HookNotSet selector
proofs.domain: m, amount unbounded; extraData length in {0,65,1024} (halmos default dynamic-bytes bounds)
proofs.nonVacuity: S1 counterexample shows the same dispatch path does NOT revert once a working hook is set; P1c proves success path reachable

proofs.claim: hook set to any symbolic h != 0, != _defaultHook (code or no code) => dispatch never reverts with HookNotSet
proofs.domain: m, h, amount unbounded; extraData length in {0,65,1024}

proofs.claim: completeness: with a working hook (incl. a FRESH DefaultDispatchHook — the documented opt-out) dispatch succeeds; guard does not over-block
proofs.domain: m, amount unbounded; extraData length in {0,65,1024}; donation disabled

proofs.claim: setHook(h) then setHook(default) re-arms the guard (HookNotSet again)
proofs.domain: m, h, amount unbounded; extraData length in {0,65,1024}

proofs.claim: hook() at deploy is non-zero, its codehash == keccak256(type(DefaultDispatchHook).runtimeCode), and it is the address the guard keys on
proofs.meaningful: partly — the codehash identity is near-concrete; the meaningful half is that the guard keys on exactly this instance

proofs.claim: after ONE arbitrary state-changing external call (symbolic selector over UniPoolerV2's non-view ABI, symbolic args, caller symbolic-or-owner), restoring hook=h0 still trips HookNotSet
proofs.meaningful: weak — byte-level immutability of an `immutable` is a compiler/EVM guarantee (no SSTORE reaches runtime code; contract has no selfdestruct/delegatecall). Value of this test is confirming no path re-keys the guard behaviourally; it is not independent evidence beyond that language guarantee.

proofs.claim: given token check passed (symbolic ordering), constructor succeeds IFF factory.getPair == pair_ (then pair()==pair_ and sUSDSIsToken0 matches ordering); otherwise reverts with exactly abi.encode(PairNotCanonical.selector, canonical, pair_)
proofs.nonVacuity: S3 counterexample canon=0xaaaa0005 (the pair) shows the success branch is reachable

proofs.claim: token0/token1 not exactly {sUSDS,phUSD} => reverts PairTokenMismatch(t0,t1) regardless of factory answer (token check precedes canonical check)

bidirectional: pair.sync() reached IFF caller's poolerAuthVersion == authVersion (symbolic authorize/bump/re-authorize schedule) AND !paused AND minPhusdOut!=0 AND minLP!=0 AND 0<sUSDSIn<=balance; unauthorized or stale callers revert with exactly Error('UniPoolerV2: caller not authorized pooler')
proofs.domain: caller, pooler, sUSDSIn, minPhusdOut, minLP, balance unbounded; auth schedule = authorize?/increment?/re-authorize? (one increment max)
proofs.nonVacuity: IFF form cannot pass vacuously; S2 counterexample shows sync reachable for authorized caller

unverified.note: Depth-2 arbitrary-call sequence. The batch (P2a,P2b,P4) was killed by `timeout 420` at 7m29s with no result emitted; P2a and P4 were then re-run alone and PASS, so the hang is attributed to P2b. NOT a halmos TIMEOUT verdict and NOT a proof — inconclusive. Depth-1 variant P2c PASSES. Needs a longer dedicated run or manual review; low concern because _defaultHook is a Solidity immutable.

notAttempted: _swapAmount / quotePool zap sizing math (sqrt + 2+ symbolic divisions — known intractable; excluded by brief)
